The BoP constitutes the power system package around the stack, which it performs thermal management, water management, and air supply management to efficiently produce electricity. In this paper, we design the concept of a low-cost slot/rack type fuel cell system for housing/building, which is easy to shape change based on intelligent BoP and tubular unit fuel cell, has high energy density per volume, and is convenient for troubleshooting.

articleTitle: 77GHz mm-wave 2 Stage CMOS Cascode Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The 77GHz millimeter-wave power amplifier(PA) is implemented in 28nm FDSOI technology. The circuit consists of a drive stage and a power stage, designed with a cascode structure using neutralization techniques and second harmonic termination. The PA is designed in a two-stage structure consisting of a drive stage and a power stage. The input, inter-stage, and output matching are designed using three transformers. The simulated saturation output power(P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) is 16.2 dBm, and the power added efficiency(PAE) is 23.7%. The simulated results show small signal gain is 23.6 dB at target frequency. The P1dB is 13.8dBm. The designed power amplifier with a supply voltage of 1.8V and consumes 61.3mW of DC power.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Four-Layer MOD Coil Array with Printed Spiral Detection Coils for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Wireless charging for small devices such as mobile electronic devices and electrical appliances has increased for a convenience. The safety as well as the charging efficiency is important in wireless charging because strong magnetic field is induced between a power transmitter and a receiver. In particular, if a metal object(MO) is between the transmitter and the receiver, it would be raised temperature by the induced magnetic field, causing a risk of burns and fires. Therefore, MO detection method is required. This paper proposes an active detection coil array for detecting MOs. Two-layer coils are configured in two stages to improve the detection performance, and each the coil is matched impedance by a series resonance at 1 MHz. Using a Korean 100 won coin as a MO, MO detection performance is confirmed according to the coil structure and coin position.

articleTitle: Copy-paste Augmentation for better saliency learning of underrepresented Object Classes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Data Augmentation plays an important role in training a better and well generalized object detection model. The publicly available object detection datasets are limited and are severely unbalanced. This leads to an inconsistent and unstable representation learning of the minority class objects. Hence, the resulting object detector model suffers from confirmation bias problem, giving a lot of inconsistent detections of minority class samples. To solve the unbalanced nature of object detection datasets we propose copy-paste augmentation method. In this method we paste the minority class samples into the images, which have no minority class samples. Our method relies on the random resizing and brightness adjustment of the selected minority sample for pasting. Our method can increase the number of samples of minority class which in turn help detector to learn better and accurate representation of the minority class objects.

articleTitle: The Implementation of Compressive Sensing Architecture for Endoscopy Image Acquisition and Reconstruction over Body-to-body Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In recent years, Compressive Sensing (CS) has a lot of outstanding applications in areas of signal processing. CS can be used to capture endoscopy images with data acquisition and reconstruction principles. This paper explains the implementation of compressive sensing in endoscopy system, aiming to facilitate efficient examination of the ears, nose, and throat (ENT) and enabling the delivery of patient disease information quickly and independently. To conduct comprehensive experiments, we use the strict testing methods involving image acquisition, Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) reconstruction, scheduling mechanism in body-to-body networks (BBN), and website development using throat image samples. Based on the results of the compressive sensing test in endoscopy images, it can be concluded that the prototype system is considered operational and suitable for future use.

articleTitle: Exploring and Creating a Physical Mechanic Rigging System – Based on SimBiCon
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study combines the principles of mechanical craftsmanship and SimBiCon simulation to create natural and dynamic character animations. By adjusting the visual effects generated by the physics engine, real-time naturalness can be achieved without programming, relying solely on 3D production software and artistic experience. In contrast to SimBiCon, this study focuses on the physical dynamics of key inverse kinematics (IK) goals as the driving force for the entire body motion. It is akin to driving the IK goals as conscious targets, while the skeletal dynamics along the IK chains automatically respond similar to the autonomic nervous system. The entire dynamic system tends to converge on a single point or minimal driving sources, creating vibrant characters with motion diffusion similar to the the central form. It can even generate interactive relationships with other characters, exhibiting smooth performance with a lower system burden. By transcending the boundaries of the intrinsic cognitive framework, this approach employs mechanical operational principles and virtual advantages to propagate freely across any point in the scene, without restrictions on distance or hierarchy, providing greater creative possibilities.

articleTitle: Enhancing Plant Disease Identification through Innovative Image Synthesis: A Study of InstaGAN and Data Augmentation in Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study explores the growing implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, particularly in agriculture, where AI-driven object detection enhances efficiency. Deep learning's potential for plant disease identification is hampered by data scarcity. To address this, data augmentation techniques like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are employed, with models like InstaGAN contributing to image synthesis. InstaGAN's innovative approach, integrating instance information and contextual preservation, is examined using the "Plant Village" dataset. The study underscores the value of InstaGAN in mitigating data limitations through synthesized image augmentation, showcasing promising outcomes in comparison to alternative models.

articleTitle: Low-Latency LeNet-5 Architecture for Handwritten Digit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of low-latency LeNet-5 architecture for real-time handwritten digit recognition. The proposed architecture comprises three convolutional layers, two max pooling layers, and a fully connected layer. Because we adopted pipeline processing between adjacent layers, the proposed architecture required roughly n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + 2n clock cycles for processing an image of n × n. For the implementation of handwritten digit recognition using 90nm complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology, the proposed LeNet-5 design of 28 × 28 input data with a 5 × 5 kernel required a gate count of roughly 7.9M, resulting in power consumption of 5.5 W at 200 MHz.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>

articleTitle: Comparison of Free-Viewpoint-Based Heterogeneous Sensor Fusion for 3D Data Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: 3D scanning and photogrammetry technologies are representative technologies for generating three-dimensional data, and they are widely used in various domains. In this paper, we explain and compare the 3D scanning, photogrammetry, and free-viewpoint-based 3D data generation technologies, followed by a comparative analysis of their empirical results.

articleTitle: Accelerating Flush Operation of LSM Tree by Leveraging the Zone Append Command
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: We propose AccelFlush, which uses the zone append command of zoned namespace (ZNS) SSD to improve the write bandwidth and scalability of the log-structured merge (LSM) tree. We configured flush_zone_group, a pre-allocated group of zones for flush operation, and leveraged the zone append command to process the flush operation without synchronization from the host side. Since the flush operation has been changed to access multiple zones simultaneously, higher bandwidth can be utilized, improving overall query-per-second. Also, even if multiple flush operations occur concurrently, append is performed only within the pre-allocated flush_zone_group, so unlike previous studies, the maximum number of flush threads does not affect the open zone limit. Through experiments, AccelFlush achieved an improvement of up to 40.3% compared to the baseline system.

articleTitle: End-of-Sentence Token Modeling for Streaming Conformer-Based Korean Children’s Speech Recognition Applied to a Social Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes an end-of-sentence (EOS) token modeling approach for streaming conformer-based Korean children’s speech recognition applied to a social robot. The baseline system for speech recognition is a streaming conformer-based speech recognition model with the joint connectionist temporal classification attention-based encoder-decoder architecture, and it is trained with the AIHub Child•Infant Free-Talk dataset. However, it is difficult to determine sentence boundaries in children’s speech because the speaking style of children is somewhat different from that of adults. Thus, the proposed approach is to insert EOS tokens into each sentence of a large children’s dataset to detect sentence boundaries. Finally, we evaluated the performance of the proposed approach on a dataset collected under scenarios of a voice interaction between children and a social robot. Consequently, the proposed EOS token modeling decreased character error rate by 1.7%, compared to the baseline.

articleTitle: Conformer-Based End-to-End Speech Recognition Using Grouped Convolution and Multi-Headed Linear Self-Attention with Headdrop
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a linear self-attention layer using a headdrop for a conformer-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) model. The proposed attention layer allows all heads to contribute to prediction with low computational complexity, compared to the self-attention-based conformer. Moreover, the convolutional module of the conformer is replaced with a grouped convolutional module to learn various representation subspaces. The proposed attention layer and grouped convolutional module are applied to a joint connectionist temporal classification attention-based encoder-decoder architecture. An ASR system employing the proposed model reduced the word error rate (WER) by 7% and 25% on test-clean of LibriSpeech, respectively, compared to those using the conformer and transformer. In addition, the ablation study reveals that the headdrop and grouped convolutional module reduce the WER.

articleTitle: Mask CycleGAN for removing artifacts in dual-energy CT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) has emerged as a promising alternative to magnetic resonance (MR) imaging for detecting bone marrow edema. However, its practical use has been limited due to the prevalent occurrence of intricate artifacts. While supervised deep learning methods can offer a solution, the absence of ground-truth images paired with each corrupted image during training poses a significant challenge. Thus, this paper proposes a novel generative network based on the CycleGAN framework. The primary objective of this network is to effectively remove artifacts and seamlessly inpaint the affected regions. The incorporation of masks as latent variables within the architecture enhances its capacity to focus on areas requiring alteration while concurrently preserving the structural fidelity of other anatomical components.

articleTitle: 3D Articulated Human Pose Recognition via Learning Deep Gaussian Mixture Models for Virtual Exercise
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a new 3D articulated human pose recognition method based on deep Gaussian mixture models is proposed for a virtual exercise game using a RGB-D camera. The proposed method acquires 3D skeleton data for each human pose with the RGB-D camera. Then, a new deep Gaussian mixture model (DGMM) is learned from 3D skeleton data for each human pose. The proposed method can recognize each 3D articulated human pose by applying the DGMM network to 3D skeleton data stream of the RGB-D camera. The performance of the proposed method is verified with real experiments.

articleTitle: Self-driving Map Creation Robot with Lidar Sensors for Smart Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper introduces a self-driving map generating robot for accurate movement of self-driving service robots in smart hospitals. The self-driving map creation robot uses the YDLIDAR X3 sensor to acquire surrounding environment information and transmits it to the map server to create a map within the hospital. The self-driving map creation robot that was actually developed was shown to create maps accurately through experiments.

articleTitle: A Study of Skin Visualization with Smartphones Using Deep Learning from Medical Cameras
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: A method is proposed to realise skin visualisation in the beauty industry using a smartphone-based consumer electronics. The smartphone is used to capture a macro image of a part of the face, while a medical camera is utilized to capture color and ultraviolet images of the same facial area. The smartphone and medical camera images are manually aligned with precision, and these images are then employed for deep learning. By utilizing a well-trained neural network, it becomes feasible to generate a UV image from the color image obtained from the smartphone. Additionally, it is also possible to convert a smartphone color image into an image that closely resembles the color image captured by a medical camera. By focusing on a specific facial region rather than the entire face, alignment becomes achievable, enabling the generation of various types of images using smartphones.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised EEG emotion recognition with Discriminative Graph Transformer Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The complexity and vulnerability to the noise of the electroencephalogram (EEG) result in uneven data distribution, leading to performance degradation in emotion recognition. To address this issue, we propose the Discriminative Graph Transformer Model (DGTM). The DGTM is designed to capture the low-dimensional manifold structures inherent in high-dimensional EEG features. This approach enables the DGTM to distinguish data points from different classes with enhanced accuracy and informativeness. To demonstrate the superior performance of our model to the limit, we conduct experiments in a semi-supervised setting, utilizing only a small amount of labeled data ranging from 2.40% to 3.99% of the total dataset. The results showed that the pro-posed DGTM outperforms state-of-the-art models in the semi-supervised setting despite the lack of available ground truth data.

articleTitle: Improvement of Tear Meniscus Measurement for Dry Eye Detection Using Smartphone and Ring Light
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: A dry eye detection method using a smartphone is proposed as one of the self-medication consumer electronics. Dry eye is detected by capturing images of the eye using a smartphone and a ring light and measuring the height of the tear meniscus. Binarization is required to compute the height of the meniscus, which indicates the tear volume, and adaptive binarization is introduced to improve on the conventional method. The performance of the binarization is improved, and a new method with a high degree of flexibility for measuring the height of the tear meniscus is investigated.

articleTitle: Denoising Capacitive Touch Sensor Noise Network with U-Net Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a denoising network for touch screen sensors, aimed at achieving high Signal-to-Noise ratio (SNR) and accurate touch detection. By utilizing the U-Net convolutional neural network (CNN), this paper introduces an effective method to reduce noise from capacitance data from touch screen sensors. Considering the capacitance data like video sequences, proposed model is trained on three adjacent frames to address noise that continuously changes over time. Through extensive evaluation, this approach demonstrates noise reduction capabilities while maintain touch signal accuracy. The dataset is composed of capacitance data with dimensions of 16 × 32, measured from the touch screen sensor. The proposed network achieves a 26 dB SNR, which is improved by 6 dB when capacitance data with an SNR of 20 dB is used as input.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient GAN Processor for Mobile Image Translation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: An energy-efficient generative adversarial network (GAN) accelerator is proposed for mobile image-to-image translation. In image translation, low precision bits below 8 were not employed due to significant output image quality degradation. In addition, due to the zero injection of transposed convolution, effective PE utilization decreased up to 89%. To address these problems, this paper proposes two key features: 1) we apply layer-wise dynamic fixed-point quantization and implement bit-combined PE to increase throughput by 2×; 2) By analyzing the matching pattern of transposed convolution, data remapping for transposed convolution that simultaneously computes 4 outputs is proposed. The proposed processor is implemented on ZCU 104 FPGA, achieving energy efficiency of 76.38 GOPS/W while consuming 6.08 W of power for mobile image-to-image translation.

articleTitle: A Comparative Evaluation on Melody Generation of Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Music has always been central to human culture. With the rise of digital tech and smart devices, its role in the Consumer Electronics (CE) sector has grown. Recently, large-scale language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT and Bard are promising to change the way we compose music. This paper explores the composing ability of Large Language Models (LLM) such as ChatGPT and Bard. Unlike older methods that required deep musical and statistical knowledge, LLM lets users simply describe what they want in music. We evaluated this LLM on how well it matches user input and the overall quality of its compositions, looking at factors like repetitiveness and scale diversity. This research aims to highlight the strengths, uses, and limits of LLM in music, setting the stage for its greater role in CE and the wider music world.Generated Melodies: https://github.com/545659928/LLMMelody

articleTitle: Virtual Hand Model Generation Through Size Modifications Of Hand Joint Feature Points for XR Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In the field of eXtended Reality (XR), Hand-based interaction, which enables immersive experiences, is a prominent medium and its importance is emerging in the realm of realistic content experience. Previous studies interacting with virtual objects typically have limitations on feeling that they are actually interacting with virtual objects , such as touching, holding, or holding them using VR Glass or a controller. In order to overcome these limitations, a hand model that can optimally interact with virtual objects while changing the size of each joint feature point of the virtual hand is proposed. The contribution of our work are, i) hand joint size variation with optimal interaction ii) virtual hand joint simulation with real environment.The usefulness of this approach has been demonstrated by testing the interaction between virtual hands and virtual objects generated based on real-time images.

articleTitle: Enhancing Image Clarity through a Comparative Analysis of Polarizing Filters and Homomorphic Filtering Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In the context of autonomous vehicles, camera-based lane recognition can be compromised by external factors like sunlight. This study evaluated two denoising methods: software-based denoising via the homomorphic filter algorithm and hardware-based denoising by attaching a polarizing filter in front of the camera lens. Images were analyzed under four conditions based on the combination of using the homomorphic filter and the presence of a polarizing filter. A comparative analysis revealed that a combined application of both filters achieved the highest Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) and the lowest Mean Square Error (MSE), establishing it as the most effective denoising approach.

articleTitle: Application of a CNN-based Acoustic Classification Model to Detecting a Target Signal with Interference
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In recent years, there have been several collapse accidents in Korea that have increased anxiety about disaster accidents. Several preliminary predictive studies have been conducted to prevent collapse accidents. Still, there are few studies on detecting survivors who need rescue after an accident. In this paper, we propose a convolutional neural networks-based abnormal sound classification model for detecting collapse survivors. The proposed model classifies nine types of sound, and its accuracy is 96.34 %. As an additional experiment, accuracy is measured for various SIR values to investigate the performance of this model when input signals are mixed with interfering signals.

articleTitle: Single-Body-Integrated Complementary Tunneling Field-Effect Transistor (SBI CTFET) and Design Consideration of Processing Margin in Dual-Gate Formation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this work, a novel single-body-integrated complementary tunneling field-effect transistor (SBI CTFET) is proposed and optimally designed by series of rigorous device simulations. The proposed device demonstrates both n-type and p-type enhancement operations free from the ambipolar characteristics of a TFET sharing the channel in common, enabling highly reliable operations and plausibly scaled cell area. The subthreshold swing (S) values for n-type and p-type in the single cell were 55 mV/dec. Moreover, the processing margin in forming its dual gates is systematically suggested for future designers.

articleTitle: Mobilint’s ARIES: Chip for Edge AI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The advancement of AI technology has led to its widespread adoption in a variety of fields. However, in the edge environment, there is currently no AI chip that effectively meets the market’s demands for performance, power efficiency, and price. As a result, AI applications have not been fully realized in edge contexts. To address this gap, we present ARIES, an innovative AI chip developed by Mobilint, a fabless company headquartered in South Korea. ARIES embodies superior performance, high power efficiency, and competitive pricing. Mobilint offers ARIES in two distinct forms: the PCIe card MLA100 and the AI box MLX-A1, each designed to maximize utility. To further enhance user engagement, a user-friendly software development kit (SDK) named qb is also provided to simplify deployment.

articleTitle: A Synthesized Voice Discrimination Method Using Characteristic Sounds Spoken by Humans
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, to prevent victimization of crimes such as impersonation fraud using synthesized voice, we propose a method to determine whether the speaker is a human or a synthesized voice using characteristic sounds spoken by humans. In our proposed method, the input voice data is first segmented into regular intervals, and the segmented data is further converted into spectrogram images. The converted images are classified into the four characteristic sounds defined in this paper using a CNN. Using the relationship between breath sounds, saliva sounds, and speech duration in human voice and synthesized voice, which were investigated in advance, the speaker of the input voice data is discriminated as human or synthesized voice. We evaluate our proposed method using actual human voice and synthesized voice generated by Japanese speech synthesis tools, and show that the proposed method shows high discrimination results.

articleTitle: Developing an Integrated Dashboard to Analyze Multimodal Data for User Experience Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The evaluation of user experience (UX) is a multifaceted process that encompasses a range of methods such as surveys, emotion recognition, and attention recognition. The effectiveness of UX evaluation depends on the integration of dependable and unbiased techniques derived from diverse user-generated data sources. In this context, we introduce a Multimodal INteractive Dashboard (MIND), a web-based platform tailored to furnish a reliable and user-centric avenue for UX evaluation. MIND incorporates three core functionalities: facial emotion recognition, EEG-based attention recognition, and image generation informed by estimated user’s poses and affective states. By seamlessly engaging users, MIND facilitates a quantitative assessment of their experiences. The proposed MIND offers multimodal data analytics and visualization to enable insights of time spans of the UX with individual users, helping improve the overall user experience.

articleTitle: Adaptive Object Detection: Balancing Accuracy and Inference Time
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Object recognition time varies based on object recognizability, from milliseconds for easy-to-recognize objects to seconds for challenging ones. Existing object detection models are constrained by fixed time limits, trading off accuracy and speed. This paper introduces novel methods that leverage mean confidence values for variable-time object detection, aiming to balance accuracy and speed. Our proposed method offers fast and accurate modes, allowing efficient initial detection while enabling accurate re-detection for low-confidence objects. The fast mode is used for easily recognizable images to save time, while accurate mode enhances accuracy for less recognizable images at the cost of utilizing more time. Using these modes together, we are able to utilize resources efficiently by saving inference time required for real-time tasks and maintaining the accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Data Concentrator Unit supported with Multiple Synchronized Cameras for Object-Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The real-time performance of Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) is crucial to swiftly analyze dynamic road conditions, make split-second decisions, and ensure passenger safety and efficient navigation in complex and ever-changing environments. Synchronized cameras play a pivotal role in AVs due to their ability to provide a multi-perspective and comprehensive view of the vehicle's surroundings. DCU (Data Concentrator Unit) is a device to collect, process, and transmit data from several sensors in AVs. In this paper, we propose Data Concentrator Unit (DCU) that is supported by Multiple Synchronized Cameras for Object-Detection. It performs object-detection analysis on multiple high-definition video streams captured by multiple synchronized cameras.

articleTitle: Data storage for efficient knowledge distillation in object detectors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: While the knowledge storage distillation method has proven effective in image classification, object detection is a considerably more complex task with numerous candidate bounding boxes. In this paper, we show that only a select few of these numerous candidate bounding boxes are pivotal for effective knowledge distillation. Consequently, we introduce a novel method that stores the features of important bounding boxes, selected based on their quality scores, and employs these features for learning using quality score-based masks. Through experiments, we demonstrate that our method significantly reduces computational overhead while preserving performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Efficiency of UDS-Based Large Data Diagnostics through CAN-FD to CAN Gateway
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The automotive industry is currently focusing on the development of vehicle software, prompting a shift in the vehicle's ECU structure from a decentralized E/E architecture to a centralized one for efficient software control. Furthermore, a domain gateway communicates with higher-level gateways through CAN-FD or Ethernet protocols and ECUs process more data than ever before. Consequently, the diagnostic framework needs to be aligned accordingly. The predominant diagnostic protocol utilized in the automotive industry is known as UDS (Unified Diagnostic Services). In the past, protocols like UDSonCAN were predominantly employed in a way that enabled gateways to bypass diagnostic messages. This present study proposes an algorithm aimed at optimizing diagnosis for large diagnostic data by converting ECU-originated CAN diagnostic messages to CAN-FD or CAN-FD-TP formats, facilitating their efficient transmission to the diagnostic tool.

articleTitle: Can Generative AI Eliminate Speech Harms? A Study on Detection of Abusive and Hate Speech during the COVID-19 Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study investigates the issue of abusive and hateful language arising from the COVID-19 pandemic, this research employs machine learning techniques to establish a system capable of detecting and rephrasing abusive and hateful language. To begin, a dataset and dictionary specific to abusive and hateful language in Chinese. Subsequently, a two-stage detection model is proposed, with the BERT model yielding the most optimal outcomes. The first stage attains an accuracy of 94.42%, while the second stage achieves an accuracy of 81.48%.

articleTitle: Development of smart glasses using an infrared distance measurement sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study provides methods of measuring the distance between the human eye and an object using an infrared distance sensor. The method provides a smart way to monitor subjects near or far vision over time using the smart device before cataract surgery. An Arduino board-based infrared distance sensor on the rim of smart glasses can measure a range of 20.00 to 80.00 centimeters as well as detect the distance from the smart glass to objects at 4 times per second.
